objects.canonical_term: Nebraska Division of Taxes for TIF
objects.summary: Core Nebraska TIF statute authorizing a redevelopment plan to divide ad valorem taxes so the base-value portion continues to normal taxing bodies and the excess/increment portion is allocated to redevelopment indebtedness for the authorized period.
objects.plain_language: The property is still taxed. The question is where the tax on the new value goes: ordinary taxing bodies receive the base portion, while the increment can repay approved redevelopment costs.

facts.object: Tax on redevelopment project valuation is paid to public bodies in the same proportion as other taxes.
Tax on value above the redevelopment project valuation is allocated to a special authority fund for bonds, loans, notes, advances, or indebtedness financing or refinancing the redevelopment project.
not more than 15 years after the effective date for most redevelopment plans
not more than 20 years if more than 50 percent of the project area has been declared extremely blighted
authority notice to county assessor on Property Tax Administrator forms on or before July 1 of the effective year
taxes remain undivided for affected years if notice is not timely satisfied

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 18-2147.
Nebraska DOR, 2025 Nebraska Legislative Changes, Community Development Law/Tax Increment Financing.

objects.canonical_term: Nebraska Expedited Review Redevelopment Plan Statute
objects.summary: Statute allowing a city, by resolution, to permit expedited review of eligible single-project redevelopment plans meeting location, age, population, value-limit, and procedural requirements.
objects.plain_language: This is the statutory basis for what people call Micro-TIF or TIF Lite.

facts.object: A city may elect by resolution to allow expedited reviews.
Eligible redevelopment plan includes only one redevelopment project.
Project must be in a substandard and blighted area and located in a county with population under 100,000.

object: repair, rehabilitation, or replacement of an existing structure in corporate limits for at least 60 years
redevelopment of a vacant lot in a substandard and blighted area in corporate limits and platted for at least 60 years

facts.object: The standard form must indicate whether the project will be financed in whole or in part through the division of taxes under sec. 18-2147.
governing body decides approve or deny within 30 days after submission
project must be completed within two years after plan approval

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 18-2155.
Nebraska DED, Micro-TIF.

objects.canonical_term: Nebraska Review of Blight and Substandard Designations
objects.summary: Authorizes a city governing body to review substandard, blighted, or extremely blighted area designations and remove a designation by resolution if the area no longer qualifies, without invalidating previously approved projects or related debt.
objects.plain_language: A city can revisit whether an old blight designation still fits, but that does not undo already-approved projects.

facts.object: governing body may review designated area at any time
governing body may remove designation by resolution if the area is no longer eligible
removal does not affect validity of approved plans, projects, bonds, contracts, or agreements approved before removal

relationships.note: Micro-TIF eligibility depends on qualifying substandard and blighted area context.

source_refs.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. sec. 18-2156.

objects.summary: Beginning January 1, 2026, restricts approval of new redevelopment plans or projects in certain areas designated substandard, blighted, or extremely blighted for more than thirty years unless the city conducts an analysis of redevelopment activity and future goals.
objects.plain_language: For very old redevelopment-area designations, a fresh analysis may be needed before new TIF-related approvals.

facts.object: area designated substandard and blighted or extremely blighted for more than 30 years

object: factors contributing to lack of redevelopment where significant redevelopment has not occurred
goals for future redevelopment of the area

facts.object: copy of analysis must be available for public inspection at a city-designated location
does not apply to downtown area of a city of the first class, city of the second class, or village

objects.canonical_term: Affordable Housing Basis TIF Approval Condition
objects.summary: For redevelopment projects using division of taxes in an area declared substandard and blighted because less than twenty percent of housing is affordable housing, approval requires residential housing construction and a finding that at least thirty percent of residential housing in the area will be affordable upon completion.
objects.plain_language: If the blight/substandard basis is lack of affordable housing, the TIF project must itself move the area toward affordable housing.

object: project includes construction of residential housing
governing body finds at least 30 percent of residential housing in the area will be affordable housing when project is complete

relationships.note: Applies to projects using division of taxes under sec. 18-2147 when affordable-housing blight basis is used.

objects.summary: Nebraska TIF mechanism splitting the tax generated by base/redevelopment project valuation from the tax generated by excess valuation above the base, with the excess used for authorized redevelopment indebtedness.
objects.plain_language: It is not a tax exemption. It is an allocation rule for property tax generated by a redevelopment project.

facts.object: excess value equals current year assessed value minus redevelopment project base value
consolidated tax rate applies to both base value and excess value
ordinary taxing subdivisions
special fund for approved redevelopment indebtedness

notify assessor, treasurer, and Property Tax Administrator when indebtedness is paid so taxes return to ordinary distribution

objects.summary: Compressed question bank for taxpayer, assessor, county board, and city/CRA questions about Nebraska TIF, with routing to canonical statutes, concepts, forms, and workflows.
objects.plain_language: These are the recurring TIF questions that need fast routing before they turn into tax confusion.

object.q: Does TIF mean the property owner does not pay property tax?
object.answer_frame: No. The property remains taxed; the increment is allocated differently under sec. 18-2147.

object.q: What does Question 6 on the Micro-TIF application mean?
object.answer_frame: It asks whether any part of project financing will use the sec. 18-2147 tax division mechanism.

object.q: What does the assessor do on a TIF project?
object.answer_frame: The assessor handles valuation/base/excess and required certifications/reports, not city redevelopment policy approval.

object.q: What happens if the notice to divide is late?
object.answer_frame: Current sec. 18-2147 and Form 96-252 direct that affected taxes remain undivided and are allocated to political subdivisions for that year.
No. It depends on city election, eligible project type, qualifying area, county population, age/platted requirements, and completed value limits.

object.q: When does a Micro-TIF applicant get money?
object.answer_frame: Local guidance often frames Micro-TIF as reimbursement after completion and after new tax value is paid; exact timing depends on local note and tax collection.

key_answer.question: Will the redevelopment project be financed in whole or in part through the division of taxes as provided in section 18-2147?
key_answer.answer: Yes means the project will use the TIF increment/division-of-taxes mechanism for all or part of project financing; no means no sec. 18-2147 tax division financing is being used.
key_answer.assessor_implication: A yes answer connects the project to base/excess valuation, Notice to Divide Tax, completion certification for expedited plans, and annual base/excess reporting.

review_notes: DED Micro-TIF page still points to a DED standard application; current DED form discovered as June 2023 reissue.
Statutory value limits in current sec. 18-2155 differ from early single-family-only guidance found in older summaries; current statute and form use $350,000, $1,500,000, and $10,000,000 caps.
Current sec. 18-2147 notice deadline is July 1 after LB240, as reflected in Form 96-252 Rev. 3-2025.
